items.name: Misquamicut State Beach
items.blurb: An Atlantic beach destination for swimming, beach days, and coastal walks, with seasonal pavilion services.

items.name: East Beach
items.blurb: A less-developed barrier beach with limited parking and fewer facilities than the larger state beaches.

items.name: Blue Shutters Town Beach
items.blurb: A municipal ocean beach with seasonal facilities. Check Charlestown’s current parking and beach-pass rules.

items.name: Charlestown Town Beach
items.blurb: An oceanfront beach near the breachway. Nonresident seasonal passes are not accepted here; consult the town’s daily-access rules.

items.name: Charlestown Breachway
items.blurb: Ocean beach and saltwater-fishing access beside the breachway.

items.name: East Matunuck State Beach
items.blurb: An ocean beach with seasonal pavilion services near the fishing village of Jerusalem.

items.name: Scarborough North State Beach
items.blurb: A substantial state beach for Atlantic surf, summer swimming, and shoreline walks.

items.name: Scarborough South State Beach
items.blurb: The southern state-beach facility adjoining Scarborough North.

items.name: Roger W. Wheeler State Beach
items.blurb: A family-oriented beach with a playground and seasonal amenities near Point Judith.

items.name: Salty Brine State Beach
items.blurb: A compact beach near the fishing docks, seafood restaurants, and Block Island ferry terminal.

items.name: Narragansett Town Beach
items.blurb: A signature surf beach near the Towers. Beach admission and parking are separate considerations; check municipal policies.

items.name: Easton’s Beach / First Beach
items.blurb: An Atlantic-facing beach at the northern end of Cliff Walk, useful for combining a beach visit with coastal sightseeing.

items.name: Sachuest Beach / Second Beach
items.blurb: A broad sandy beach with swimming and surfing areas. Check which parking areas accept nonresidents.

items.name: Third Beach
items.blurb: A quieter cove beach. Seasonal parking restrictions apply, including resident-only lots.

items.name: South Shore Beach
items.blurb: A coastal beach offering open Atlantic views and a quieter rural setting. Municipal parking charges and seasonal services apply.

items.name: Goosewing Beach
items.blurb: A beach and nature preserve reached on foot from South Shore Beach. Respect nesting-bird closures and marked habitat boundaries.

items.name: Mackerel Cove
items.blurb: Jamestown’s town beach, suitable for a beach-and-village outing. Parking is limited and seasonal rules apply.

items.name: Oakland Beach
items.blurb: A neighborhood waterfront destination for shoreline views and nearby clam-shack dining. Check current swimming advisories before entering the water.

items.name: Fred Benson Town Beach
items.blurb: A town-operated beach along Crescent Beach, with seasonal concessions, rentals, and visitor facilities.

items.name: Mohegan Bluffs
items.blurb: A dramatic coastal overlook above the Atlantic. Check stairway and beach-access notices; erosion has caused restrictions at the bottom of the stairs. Access notice: https://dem.ri.gov/press-releases/bottom-mohegan-bluffs-staircase-block-island-closed-until-further-notice-due-erosion

items.name: Beavertail State Park
items.blurb: Rocky shoreline, ocean panoramas, walking routes, and lighthouse scenery. Particularly useful for a coastal sightseeing outing.

items.name: Fort Wetherill State Park
items.blurb: Former coastal defenses, wooded paths, coves, and elevated water views. Follow posted boundaries around the fortifications and cliffs.

items.name: Fort Getty Park
items.blurb: A town-owned waterfront park with old fortifications, shoreline, a boat ramp, and views across the West Passage.

items.name: Fort Adams State Park
items.blurb: Harbor views, waterfront grounds, and access to the historic fortress. Interior fort tours are a separate attraction.

items.name: Brenton Point State Park
items.blurb: Ocean-facing open space along Ocean Drive, suited to picnics, kite watching, and coastal views.

items.name: Colt State Park
items.blurb: Waterfront lawns, paths, picnic areas, and bay scenery. A useful anchor for a Bristol day trip.

items.name: Haines Memorial State Park
items.blurb: A waterfront park with picnic space and boating access near the East Bay Bike Path.

items.name: Goddard Memorial State Park
items.blurb: A large coastal park with woodland trails, picnic grounds, a beach, and recreation facilities.

items.name: Rocky Point State Park
items.blurb: Bayfront walking and open space on the former amusement-park property, with a public fishing pier.

items.name: Lincoln Woods State Park
items.blurb: Woodland recreation surrounding Olney Pond, with walking, paddling, and mountain-biking opportunities.

items.name: Pulaski State Park
items.blurb: Woodland recreation, trails, and a freshwater beach in northwestern Rhode Island.

items.name: Snake Den State Park
items.blurb: An undeveloped park with woodland trails and a working-farm landscape.

items.name: Roger Williams Park
items.blurb: A major city park containing gardens, ponds, walking areas, the zoo, and several separately operated attractions.

items.name: Slater Memorial Park
items.blurb: A large municipal park with recreation facilities, historic carousel, gardens, picnic areas, and connections to the Ten Mile River Greenway.

items.name: Ninigret Park
items.blurb: A municipal recreation destination with open space and access to the Frosty Drew campus. Distinct from neighboring Ninigret National Wildlife Refuge.

items.name: Cliff Walk
items.blurb: A 3.5-mile coastal walk combining ocean scenery and mansion views. Terrain varies; it is not uniformly paved or accessible. Note: The city posts a detour between Narragansett Avenue and Webster Street.

items.name: Sachuest Point National Wildlife Refuge
items.blurb: Coastal walking and birdwatching, especially valuable for migratory and wintering birds. Storms can affect the access road.

items.name: Trustom Pond National Wildlife Refuge
items.blurb: Walking, wildlife photography, and birdwatching through varied coastal habitats. Location note: The visitor entrance is on Matunuck Schoolhouse Road in South Kingstown.

items.name: Ninigret National Wildlife Refuge
items.blurb: Salt-pond and woodland exploration, including trails associated with the Kettle Pond Visitor Center. Note: The Salt Pond Unit is scheduled to close November 14–15, 2026, for the Veterans Deer Hunt.

items.name: Block Island National Wildlife Refuge
items.blurb: Coastal habitat and wildlife observation, with particularly strong migratory-bird interest.

items.name: Neutaconkanut Hill
items.blurb: An urban woodland escape with trails, elevated views, and recreation facilities in the Silver Lake neighborhood.

items.name: Weetamoo Woods
items.blurb: A substantial trail network through woodland and historic rural landscapes. Expect roots, rocks, and seasonally wet sections.

items.name: Claire D. Mcintosh Wildlife Refuge
items.blurb: Walking and wildlife observation.

items.name: Davis Memorial Wildlife Refuge
items.blurb: Nature walks and birdwatching.

items.name: Emilie Ruecker Wildlife Refuge
items.blurb: Quiet walks and wildlife observation.

items.name: Fisherville Brook Wildlife Refuge
items.blurb: Hiking and nature photography.

items.name: Fort Wildlife Refuge
items.blurb: Woodland hiking and birdwatching.

items.name: George B. Parker Woodland
items.blurb: Woodland walks and nature study.

items.name: Lathrop Wildlife Refuge
items.blurb: Walking and birdwatching.

items.name: Lewis-Dickens Farm Wildlife Refuge
items.blurb: Island walking and wildlife observation.

items.name: Long Pond Woods
items.blurb: Woodland hiking and nature study.

items.name: Maxwell Mays Wildlife Refuge
items.blurb: Walking and wildlife observation.

items.name: Powder Mill Ledges Wildlife Refuge
items.blurb: Nature walks and birdwatching.

items.name: Touisset Marsh Wildlife Refuge
items.blurb: Walking and wildlife observation.

items.name: Waterman Pond Wildlife Refuge
items.blurb: Nature exploration; expect rougher conditions.

items.name: East Bay Bike Path
items.blurb: Paved shared-use path. Approximately 14.5 miles. India Point Park to Independence Park, passing through East Providence, Barrington, and Warren. Bay views, village stops, and longer recreational rides. Note: This path does not continue to Newport.

items.name: Washington Secondary Bike Path
items.blurb: Paved rail-trail. Approximately 19 miles. Longer inland rides through Cranston, Warwick, West Warwick, and Coventry. Note: Cranston Bike Path, Warwick Bike Path, West Warwick Greenway, Coventry Greenway, and Trestle Trail are sections of this corridor, not five unrelated trails.

items.name: Blackstone River Bikeway
items.blurb: Separated path plus connecting on-road and off-road segments. RIDOT describes an 18.2-mile network, including an 11.6-mile path between Cumberland and Woonsocket. River scenery and industrial-history outings. Some segments share the road with traffic.

items.name: William C. O’neill / South County Bike Path
items.blurb: Paved shared-use path. Approximately 7.8 miles. Kingston Station toward Mumford Road in Narragansett, with a separate URI connector. A rail-trail outing through South County.

items.name: Ten Mile River Greenway
items.blurb: Paved shared-use greenway. Approximately 3 miles. A shorter ride near Slater Park and the James V. Turner Reservoir. Note: The route includes rolling terrain.

items.name: Quonset / Davisville Bike Path
items.blurb: Separated paved path. Approximately 3.7 miles. Post Road toward the Calf Pasture Point area. A relatively short recreational ride with coastal access nearby.

items.name: Fred Lippitt Woonasquatucket River Greenway
items.blurb: Mixed on-road and off-road route. Approximately 5 miles in RIDOT’s description. Urban cycling and connections through the Woonasquatucket corridor. Note: Road sections and busy crossings require traffic awareness.

items.name: Newport Bike Path
items.blurb: Off-road urban path network. Nearly 3 miles including its spur. Connections between the North End, CCRI area, and Newport Gateway Center. Note: This does not provide bicycle access across the Pell Bridge.

items.name: Warren Bike Path
items.blurb: Short paved rail-trail. Approximately 1 mile. Eastern Warren between the Kickemuit area and Long Lane. Note: Connections to the East Bay Bike Path involve streets.

items.name: Burrillville Bike Path
items.blurb: Paved rail-trail. Approximately 1.2 miles. Pascoag to Harrisville. A shorter ride through woods and wetlands.

items.name: Colt State Park Cycling Paths
items.blurb: Paved park paths and connecting routes. Waterfront recreational cycling and shorter loops within a larger park outing. Note: This is a park cycling network, not a separate long-distance rail-trail.

items.name: Warwick City Park / Buttonwoods Paths
items.blurb: Paved municipal park paths. The city identifies approximately 3 miles of paved bicycle paths. Short rides combined with playgrounds, picnic areas, and shoreline scenery.

items.name: Arcadia Management Area
items.blurb: A large forest network with mountain biking and other outdoor recreation.

items.name: Big River Management Area
items.blurb: An extensive, interconnected trail system; navigation preparation is particularly useful.

items.name: Burlingame
items.blurb: Singletrack and woodland riding near the park and campground.

items.name: Lincoln Woods
items.blurb: Rocky woodland riding with technical features and varied route choices.

items.name: Diamond Hill
items.blurb: Cross-country and technical riding, including advanced jumps and drops.

items.name: Woody Hill
items.blurb: Trails ranging from approachable riding to more technical terrain.

items.name: Ryan Park
items.blurb: Generally gentler trails that can suit newer mountain bikers.

items.name: Carolina Management Area
items.blurb: Gravel and cross-country riding, with some more technical trail options.

items.name: Beavertail Lighthouse Museum
items.blurb: Maritime history at one of Rhode Island’s defining coastal landmarks. Museum hours are seasonal; tower climbs occur only on announced dates.

items.name: Rose Island Lighthouse
items.blurb: An offshore lighthouse visit requiring transport arrangements. Overnight stays are also offered through the lighthouse organization.

items.name: Watch Hill Lighthouse
items.blurb: Walk to the lighthouse property from the village. The museum is seasonal; the tower and adjacent structures are not generally open.

items.name: North Light
items.blurb: A lighthouse and seasonal interpretive museum reached by walking along the shore near the island’s northern tip. Note: The town lists the museum as closed after Columbus Day.

items.name: Southeast Lighthouse
items.blurb: A landmark near Mohegan Bluffs with seasonal museum and guided tower visits. Note: The published schedule lists winter closure; grounds have separate access hours.

items.name: Pomham Rocks Lighthouse
items.blurb: An offshore lighthouse visited through the Friends’ escorted boat tours. Note: Closed for the season. Private boat, canoe, and kayak landings are not permitted.

items.name: Point Judith Lighthouse
items.blurb: A coastal landmark at an active Coast Guard station. Treat this as a viewing destination; do not promise tower or station-ground access.

items.name: Conimicut Lighthouse View
items.blurb: View the offshore lighthouse from Conimicut Point Park or the water. The lighthouse itself is not a walk-in attraction.

items.name: The Breakers
items.blurb: The Vanderbilt mansion and a central introduction to Newport’s Gilded Age architecture. Note: Terrace restoration affects portions of the exterior visitor experience.

items.name: Marble House
items.blurb: A Vanderbilt house emphasizing monumental architecture and elaborate interiors.

items.name: The Elms
items.blurb: A mansion with formal gardens and historic household technology. Note: The operator announces reopening November 16, 2026, with a new timed-ticket experience.

items.name: Rosecliff
items.blurb: Architecture, a grand ballroom, and changing exhibitions. Consult the current exhibition and opening calendar.

items.name: Kings Cote / Kingscote
items.blurb: A Gothic Revival house representing an earlier phase of Newport’s summer-estate development. Note: Listed as closed for the season.

items.name: Chateau-Sur-Mer
items.blurb: A Victorian house with elaborate decorative interiors. Note: The operator announces reopening November 21, 2026.

items.name: Rough Point Museum
items.blurb: Doris Duke’s former home, with art, interiors, and coastal grounds interpreted by the Newport Restoration Foundation.

items.name: Lippitt House Museum
items.blurb: A preserved Victorian home interpreting industry, immigration, design, and domestic life. Tours follow a limited seasonal calendar.

items.name: The Museum at the John Brown House
items.blurb: A historic house used to explore Rhode Island’s social, commercial, and family history.

items.name: Museum of Work & Culture
items.blurb: The stories of immigrants, workers, and families in the Blackstone Valley’s industrial communities.

items.name: Old Slater Mill
items.blurb: National Park Service interpretation of early textile manufacturing and the changes brought by industrialization. Note: Tour seasons vary; neighboring historic buildings may have separate closures.

items.name: Smith’s Castle
items.blurb: A historic house and waterfront landscape interpreting four centuries of Rhode Island history, including its plantation past.

items.name: Gilbert Stuart Birthplace & Museum
items.blurb: The restored Stuart family home, mill setting, and exhibits about the portrait artist. Regular visits are seasonal.

items.name: South County Museum
items.blurb: Rural, coastal, craft, and village history on the Canonchet Farm grounds. Note: Regular 2026 seasonal operation has ended; consult special programs and group-visit arrangements.

items.name: Newport Historical Society Museum & Tours
items.blurb: Exhibitions and walking tours exploring Newport’s history beyond the mansion district.

items.name: Fort Adams Interior Tours
items.blurb: Guided or self-guided exploration of the coastal fortress, with access determined by the selected tour.

items.name: Seabee Museum & Memorial Park
items.blurb: Quonset huts, artifacts, and exhibits at the original Rhode Island home of the Navy’s Seabees.

items.name: New England Wireless & Steam Museum
items.blurb: Historic steam machinery and early wireless technology. Note: Regular 2026 Saturday opening dates ended October 24; check special events.

items.name: Clouds Hill Museum
items.blurb: A Victorian house, carriage collection, and grounds. Visits take place during announced openings or by appointment.

items.name: Touro Synagogue
items.blurb: A major site in American Jewish history and religious liberty. Public tours require registration and follow a specific calendar.

items.name: First Baptist Church in America
items.blurb: A historic meetinghouse connected to Roger Williams and the history of religious liberty. Consult the church’s own tour arrangements.

items.name: Hearthside House / Great Road Heritage Campus
items.blurb: Historic-house interpretation and related heritage buildings presented through scheduled tours and programs.

items.name: Risd Museum
items.blurb: Art and design collections with changing exhibitions, public programs, and substantial indoor exploration.

items.name: Newport Art Museum
items.blurb: Historic buildings, regional and contemporary art, exhibitions, and educational programs.

items.name: Jamestown Arts Center
items.blurb: A nonprofit destination for exhibitions, classes, performances, films, and artist talks.

items.name: Warwick Center for the Arts
items.blurb: Local and regional art exhibitions, classes, workshops, and community programs in Apponaug.

items.name: As220
items.blurb: An independent nonprofit arts organization offering galleries, performances, workshops, and community creative spaces.

items.name: Waterfire & Waterfire Arts Center
items.blurb: Downtown river installations on announced lighting dates, plus exhibitions and programs at the Arts Center. Note: WaterFire is not a nightly attraction.

items.name: Blithewold
items.blurb: A historic mansion, gardens, and arboretum offering seasonal horticultural interest and special programs. Note: Mansion access can change for private events.

items.name: Green Animals Topiary Garden
items.blurb: A seasonal garden attraction known for sculpted plant forms and its historic coastal setting.

items.name: Roger Williams Park Botanical Center
items.blurb: Indoor greenhouses and outdoor gardens offering a useful cold-weather or rainy-day outing.

items.name: Swan Point Cemetery
items.blurb: A historic garden cemetery welcoming quiet exploration under its visitor rules. Note: Respect services and graveside privacy; photography restrictions apply.

items.name: Roger Williams Park Zoo
items.blurb: Animal habitats, educational programs, and separately scheduled seasonal attractions.

items.name: Providence Children’s Museum
items.blurb: Hands-on learning and play designed especially for children and their accompanying adults.

items.name: Biomes Marine Biology Center
items.blurb: A private marine-education attraction focused on New England marine life and hands-on learning.

items.name: Save the Bay’s Hamilton Family Aquarium
items.blurb: Marine-life exhibits and interactive learning focused on Narragansett Bay.

items.name: Audubon Nature Center & Aquarium
items.blurb: Indoor nature exhibits and marine life, with outdoor exploration at the associated refuge.

items.name: Crescent Park Looff Carousel
items.blurb: A historic carousel and local preservation landmark. Check the seasonal operating calendar.

items.name: Flying Horse Merry-Go-Round
items.blurb: A historic seasonal children’s carousel in the village. Check current rider restrictions and opening dates.

items.name: Museum of Natural History & Planetarium
items.blurb: Natural-history exhibits in Roger Williams Park, with separately scheduled planetarium programs.

items.name: Frosty Drew Observatory & Science Center
items.blurb: Public astronomy programs at Ninigret Park. Telescope viewing depends on weather, and some sessions require tickets.

items.name: Norman Bird Sanctuary
items.blurb: Trails, nature programs, and a hands-on Curiosity Lab. Check in at the Welcome Center before hiking. Note: Dogs and trail cycling are prohibited; service-animal provisions apply.

items.name: Block Island Ferry
items.blurb: The principal Rhode Island ferry gateway to Block Island. Choose the appropriate passenger or vehicle service and check current departures.

items.name: Prudence & Bay Islands Transport
items.blurb: Ferry service connecting Bristol and Prudence Island. Vehicle reservations and the current seasonal timetable require advance attention.

items.name: Jamestown Newport Ferry
items.blurb: Seasonal passenger transportation linking waterfront destinations. Check which stops and services operate on the chosen date.

items.name: Coastal Queen / Cruise RI
items.blurb: Scenic and themed cruises with departure points varying by trip. Consult the specific cruise listing.

items.name: Providence River Boat Company
items.blurb: Narrated river tours offering views of downtown from the water. Note: Confirm boarding arrangements and accessibility directly with the operator.

items.name: La Gondola
items.blurb: Private Venetian-style gondola trips along the downtown waterways, with seasonal and special-event options.

items.name: Gansett Cruises
items.blurb: Narrated harbor and bay cruises, including seasonal sunset departures.

items.name: Schooner Madeleine
items.blurb: Day and sunset sailing aboard a traditional-style schooner on Newport Harbor and Narragansett Bay.

items.name: Blackstone Valley Explorer
items.blurb: River tours interpreting the valley’s ecology and industrial heritage. Departure locations and schedules are program-specific.

items.name: Save the Bay Seal & Nature Tours
items.blurb: Seasonal wildlife trips interpreting harbor seals and the bay’s environment. Note: Wildlife sightings are not guaranteed; confirm the departure port.

items.name: Allen Harbor Access
items.blurb: A municipal access point for exploring the harbor and connected bay waters.

items.name: Wilson Park Water Access
items.blurb: A waterfront park and launch area useful for Wickford-oriented boating outings.

items.name: Haines Memorial Boat Ramp
items.blurb: A public launch serving the upper bay area.

items.name: Colt State Park Boating Access
items.blurb: Water access within the larger park setting. Consult the current launch map and facility information.

items.name: Alton Pond Landing
items.blurb: A launch serving Alton Pond and the Wood River corridor.

items.name: Upper Wood River Paddling Route
items.blurb: A mapped river outing from the Route 165 area toward Wyoming Pond. Note: The full mapped trip includes a portage at Barberville Dam.

items.name: Worden Pond Access
items.blurb: A public launch on a large freshwater pond. Open-water wind conditions matter when planning a paddle.

items.name: Olney Pond
items.blurb: Freshwater paddling within Lincoln Woods State Park, with coves and islands to explore.

items.name: Larry Mouradjian Fishing Pier
items.blurb: The public fishing pier at Rocky Point State Park, with accessible design features.

items.name: Galilee Fishing Piers
items.blurb: Saltwater pier fishing near the working port and Galilee breachway area.

items.name: Stone Bridge Pier
items.blurb: Shore-based fishing beside the Grinnell’s Beach area on the Sakonnet River.

items.name: Carbuncle Pond
items.blurb: An inland freshwater fishing destination included in DEM’s trout-water resources.

items.name: Meadow Brook Pond
items.blurb: A freshwater fishing destination identified in DEM’s stocking information.

items.name: Stafford Pond
items.blurb: A freshwater fishing option in the East Bay region. Consult DEM’s current water-specific information.

items.name: Shippee Sawmill Pond
items.blurb: A rural freshwater fishing destination included in DEM’s fall stocking program.

items.name: Casey Farm
items.blurb: A working historic farm with educational programs, farm interpretation, and a seasonal market.

items.name: Watson Farm
items.blurb: A working coastal farm offering seasonal self-guided landscape visits. Note: The farmhouse is a private residence; regular 2026 walking-tour dates ended October 15.

items.name: Wright’s Dairy Farm & Bakery
items.blurb: A multigenerational working dairy farm with a bakery and creamery. Note: Distinct from Wright’s Farm Restaurant in Burrillville.

items.name: Jaswell’s Farm
items.blurb: A family farm with a market, bakery, cider, and seasonal pick-your-own activities. Note: Crop availability changes; verify picking conditions before traveling.

items.name: Steere Orchard
items.blurb: A longstanding orchard offering seasonal fruit and pick-your-own opportunities.

items.name: Salisbury Farm
items.blurb: A local farm destination for seasonal produce and farm activities. Confirm which activities are operating.

items.name: Narrow Lane Orchard
items.blurb: A local orchard at 213 Narrow Lane. Check the current crop and visiting schedule.

items.name: Confreda Greenhouses & Farms
items.blurb: A family agricultural business with a farm market, produce, plants, and seasonal activities. Location note: The market is in western Cranston despite its Hope mailing address.

items.name: Farm Fresh RI Winter Farmers Market
items.blurb: An indoor gathering of local farms and food producers at 10 Sims Avenue. 2026–27 schedule: Saturdays, November 7 through April 24, 9 a.m.–1 p.m.

items.name: Hope Street Farmers Market
items.blurb: A seasonal outdoor market at Lippitt Park featuring local growers and food producers. Note: Use the market’s own current calendar; do not assume year-round outdoor operation.

items.name: Gray’s Ice Cream
items.blurb: A longstanding local ice-cream business, with its Tiverton shop anchoring the Four Corners area.

items.name: Brickley’s Ice Cream
items.blurb: A local ice-cream destination on Main Street, useful as part of a Wakefield or South County outing.

items.name: Three Sisters
items.blurb: Homemade ice cream on Hope Street, with year-round service advertised by the business.

items.name: The Inside Scoop
items.blurb: A local homemade-ice-cream shop on Ten Rod Road. Note: Official site says closed for the 2026 season, returning in spring 2027.

items.name: Lincoln Creamery
items.blurb: A family-owned neighborhood ice-cream stop serving the Blackstone Valley. Note: Confirm current hours; its homepage retains older seasonal wording.

items.name: Clemmie’s Homemade Ice Cream
items.blurb: The locally owned business formerly called Clementine’s. Note: Official site says closed for the 2026 season.

items.name: Holy Cow
items.blurb: A local ice-cream stop with traditional and alternative frozen-dessert choices.

items.name: Cold Fusion Gelato
items.blurb: A seasonal Thames Street gelato and sorbet destination.

items.name: Pastiche Fine Desserts
items.blurb: A longstanding Federal Hill bakery for cakes, tarts, and other desserts. Service note: The business describes itself as takeout-only.

items.name: Allie’s Donuts
items.blurb: A Rhode Island doughnut institution at 3661 Quaker Lane, useful for a local-food stop on a South County trip.

items.name: 100 most-loved Rhode Island restaurants
items.blurb: Our full list of independent restaurants, clam shacks, diners and bakeries lives in the business directory on every page. Pick "Restaurants" in the directory menu.

items.name: Wickford Village
items.blurb: Harbor scenery, independent shops, galleries, gifts, and food stops in a compact historic village.

items.name: Downtown Bristol
items.blurb: Historic streets, waterfront scenery, and local storefronts around Hope Street and the harbor.

items.name: Downtown Warren
items.blurb: A walkable East Bay district with shops, galleries, restaurants, and waterfront character.

items.name: Tiverton Four Corners
items.blurb: A rural village cluster of shops, galleries, local food, and artisan businesses.

items.name: Chepachet Village
items.blurb: Historic buildings, antiques, country-store shopping, and nearby rural outings.

items.name: Downtown Westerly
items.blurb: Independent shopping and dining near Wilcox Park, with a compact town-center atmosphere.

items.name: Watch Hill Village
items.blurb: A coastal village for seasonal shops, harbor views, and walks toward the lighthouse.

items.name: Hope Street
items.blurb: Neighborhood shops, locally made gifts, food businesses, and independent retail.

items.name: Westminster Street
items.blurb: Downtown independent retail, books, design, gifts, and nearby cultural destinations.

items.name: Main Street
items.blurb: A traditional downtown shopping and dining district with nearby waterfront streets.

items.name: Burlingame State Campground
items.blurb: A large woodland campground near Watchaug Pond and other South County outdoor destinations. Note: Check current construction and facility notices.

items.name: Fishermen’s Memorial State Campground
items.blurb: Tent and RV camping near Point Judith, state beaches, and the Block Island ferry.

items.name: George Washington State Campground
items.blurb: A wooded camping setting near Bowdish Reservoir, with a more rustic outdoor emphasis.

items.name: Charlestown Breachway Camping
items.blurb: A coastal camping option for self-contained vehicles; check the state’s camping requirements before booking.

items.name: East Beach Camping
items.blurb: A specialized barrier-beach camping option with vehicle, equipment, and access requirements. Note: Check the state’s requirements before including it in an itinerary.

items.name: Fort Getty Campground
items.blurb: Town-operated waterfront camping with distinct tent and RV arrangements. Note: The town lists camping as closed; RV sites involve assignment and waitlist procedures. Tent information: https://www.jamestownri.gov/tentsitereservations

items.name: Melville Ponds Campground
items.blurb: A camping base on Aquidneck Island, with the town directing visitors to the campground’s current operator website.
